description: Recover an unknown universal-object (apex) dimension from noisy cones. Product of k in {2,3} factors, random dims; true apex dim D unknown to the method. #fit = how many candidate apex dims factor the data (existence ambiguity: a whole range [D..] fits). Accuracy = recovers the true D exactly (Wilson 95% CI).
reading_note: EXISTENCE is ambiguous (#fit > 1: many over-complete apexes factor the data), so 'mint the biggest object that fits' (EXISTENCE-naive) mints a weak/over-complete limit and fails. The CERTIFICATE (uniqueness margin = d_L-th singular value above a fixed relative threshold) recovers the true unknown dimension with no knowledge of sigma, and the minted subspace factors held-out (OOD) cones. Occam-smallest also lands on D but only by a tie-break; the certificate gives the principled reason (uniqueness of the mediator). In the linear case this criterion is exactly a spectral-gap rank test -- elementary, but it is the defensible kernel of 'minting by universal property', made noise-robust.
